pr_title: Provide options for tests to filter out particular API errors
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature
/sig scheduling

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

We used to have universal functions to bypass particular API errors and then retry. This behavior was mutated in #95495 - in that PR's discussion, it's more preferable to fail the error early, and leave the error filtering decision to client instead of a one-off function.

In terms of scheduler performance testing, it doesn't really care about transient API errors. As described in #96651, it's not favorable to abort the whole test upon a single tolerable API error. So this PR adds an option for tests to be able to filter out particular API errors.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #96651

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

Note that, apart from `CreatePod()`, this PR doesn't apply the option to all other `CreateXYZ` functions.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

Retrying requests that potentially already mutated state is a bad practice.  If a particular test needs/wants to ignore errors and retry under those conditions, I could see it on a case by case basis.  However, for this particular issue, it seems that the test may have simply alerted you to the fact that you are not scaling to where you want and the cluster will start timing out requests.  If that's the case (and it seems reasonably likely to be), then even targeting this to your individual test may not be what you want.

> If a particular test needs/wants to ignore errors and retry under those conditions, I could see it on a case by case basis.

+1 on it's a case by case basis. As mentioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96696#discussion_r527295616, the motivation of this PR is to relax the perf test when preparing a large number (5k) of Pods, as a retry can be safely caught by the `AlreadyExists` err check if the previous timed-out req has succeeded, and also it only impacts the client (scheduler perf test) instead of general helper functions, so I think providing extra options can be beneficial.

issue_context.title: [scheduler_perf] Transient API error aborts the scheduler perf test
issue_context.body:
In recent testings using [scheduler_perf](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/integration/scheduler_perf), I encountered the following error which aborts the entire test suite:

```
--- FAIL: BenchmarkPerfScheduling/SchedulingPodAntiAffinity/500Nodes
    scheduler_perf_test.go:366: op 2: Error creating pod: Failed to create object with non-retriable error: The POST operation against Pod could not be completed at this time, please try again.
```

The source comes from API machinery code:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6dddea5abfa20a22e93114d66735441f04f4a39c/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors/errors.go#L314-L329

According to the comment, upon this transient API error, we should retry the request instead of quit and abort the whole test.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-longterm

@Huang-Wei https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96061 merged three days ago. Although  `NewServerTimeout(..)` is not thrown by the request timeout logic. You will see a `504` from the server with the following message:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L56
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/rest.go#L267

It just makes me curious with the timing of the test failure and the PR merge.

Thanks @yue9944882, I didn't think it was P&F but I wasn't certain we failed too-long requests via a different code path.

I think there's still a way we could have made this slightly worse, though, imagine a request sat in our queue for the max of 15 seconds. Imagine this request will take 55 seconds to complete. From the perspective of the global time out, it will take 55+15 = 70 seconds and be failed with this message (70 > 60). Without APF it theoretically might have succeeded, if nothing else changed.

...However, we expect a server that's taking that long to process a request is probably timing out random requests and is not actually that healthy, so I wouldn't really consider this a bug unless we've got requests that take more than 45 seconds for an unburdened control plane to process (we really should not).

review_comments: We'd better to fix all other methods since this is problem for all the `CreatexxxWithRetries` method, not just Pod creation, actually, the retry is not effective at all.

I could be ok with retrying this error, but retrying on timeouts in a generic helper like this is not correct.

You could update a perf test to retry, but not a generic helper that people will assume is safe and reasonable for e2e tests.

Note that this PR doesn't change any default behavior - it only provides extra options for client to customize the behavior upon errors. And to be conservative, I'd like to start with `CreatePod()` only.

> Note that this PR doesn't change any default behavior - it only provides extra options for client to customize the behavior upon errors. And to be conservative, I'd like to start with `CreatePod()` only.

I don't think this option should be available to general test authors using these utilities.  We've seen abuse (inconsistent abuse even), in the past.  Finding a way to wrap  this in ` test/integration/scheduler_perf` is preferable.
+1 on doing the reties in scheduler_perf
